title: AI has made the lives of chip designers harder, not easier
gist: A forum post from a Design Automation Conference attendee argues that AI has net-increased the difficulty of chip design: experienced silicon engineers still do not trust AI to design chips, while AI silicon itself forces harder verification, multiphysics and power-closure problems than the productivity gains offset.

insights.claim: Most experienced silicon engineers at the Design Automation Conference do not yet completely trust AI to design chips, despite vendor messaging to the contrary.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Practitioner trust, not model capability, is the gating variable for AI-EDA revenue — discount seat-count projections that assume fast adoption.
insights.quote: I noticed that most experienced silicon engineers do not completely trust AI to design chips quite yet.
insights.locator: There, I noticed that most experienced

insights.claim: AI's concrete benefit in chip design so far is narrow productivity and quality-of-life gains such as vibe coding RTL, not end-to-end design automation.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Value accrues to tools that assist within existing flows; be skeptical of startups pricing on full-flow replacement.
insights.quote: AI does offer some productivity and quality of life benefits for chip designers, such as vibe coding RTL

insights.claim: Silicon built for AI applications requires increasingly complex architectures and compute, so AI as a workload is adding more design difficulty than AI as a tool is removing.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: The engineering-headcount-deflation thesis for AI in EDA may be backwards; design services and verification demand can grow even as AI tools spread.
insights.quote: quite paradoxically, silicon for AI applications requires increasingly complex architectures and compute requirements

insights.claim: Verification, historically the most labor-intensive step in chip design, is becoming more complex rather than less as AI silicon scales.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Verification remains the largest EDA spend pool and the highest-leverage place for AI tooling to be monetized — watch DV-focused vendors.
insights.quote: More complex verification, which has historically been the most labor-intensive step in chip design

insights.claim: Off-chip thermal, signal-integrity, power-integrity and packaging multiphysics have become a distinct bottleneck class in AI chip design, pushing difficulty outside the die boundary.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Multiphysics and packaging-aware simulation tools sit on the growth vector; die-centric point tools do not.

insights.claim: Bursty, unpredictable LLM workloads running on systolic arrays are causing late-stage firefighting in power closure, a failure mode created by the workload itself.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Workload-driven power volatility raises tape-out schedule risk for AI accelerator startups — a hidden source of slipped silicon dates.
insights.quote: Late-stage firefighting in power closure due to bursty, unpredictable LLM workloads in systolic arrays
